name: Crane Trust Nature & Visitor Center
publicStatus: Public visitor center; guided riverfront experiences require booking
summary: Best first stop for orientation, current local information, exhibits and access to Crane Trust guided crane experiences.
whatToExpect: Visitor center, migration interpretation, nature trails and an observation tower. During March, guided riverfront blinds, daytime driving tours and footbridge experiences are offered separately.
visitTip: If this is your first crane trip, start here before choosing a roadside or river viewing site. Staff can provide current local viewing guidance.
permit: No general visitor-center permit stated; guided experiences are ticketed and should be reserved ahead during crane season
parking: On-site visitor parking at the Nature & Visitor Center
accessibility: Visitor center is a strong accessibility-oriented starting point; verify accommodations for the specific guided experience you book
address: 9325 S Alda Rd, Wood River, NE 68883

name: Richard Plautz Crane Viewing Site
summary: One of the easiest free self-guided river-viewing choices near Gibbon, with dedicated parking and elevated decks.
whatToExpect: Two elevated wooden viewing decks, a roughly 1,650-foot paved trail and a paved parking lot at the Elm Island Road / Lowell Road area south of I-80 Exit 285.
visitTip: A strong no-reservation choice for dawn or dusk. Use the designated lot and platform rather than stopping along the road.
permit: No permit requirement identified by Central Platte NRD for the viewing site
accessibility: Central Platte NRD lists handicap facilities; the site includes a paved trail and parking
address: Elm Island Rd & Lowell Rd area, south of Gibbon, NE 68840

name: Alda Crane Viewing Site
summary: A free, upgraded viewing site south of the Alda interchange with paved parking and an accessible concrete route to the river platform.
whatToExpect: A rebuilt viewing platform, approximately 1,047 feet of wide concrete trail and three paved parking areas. The site is about two miles south of I-80 Exit 305.
visitTip: Pair this with a stop at the nearby Crane Trust visitor center for current migration information before heading to the river around dawn or dusk.
permit: No permit requirement identified by Central Platte NRD for the viewing site
parking: Three paved parking areas are part of the upgraded site
accessibility: Central Platte NRD describes the upgraded site as fully ADA accessible
address: Alda Rd at the Platte River, about 2 miles south of I-80 Exit 305, Alda, NE

name: Iain Nicolson Audubon Center at Rowe Sanctuary
publicStatus: Sanctuary; guided crane-viewing access is controlled/reservation-based
summary: The most immersive reservation-based crane experience in the Gibbon area and the home of the Rowe live crane camera.
whatToExpect: Audubon visitor center and sanctuary plus crane-season guided sunrise and sunset experiences. Specialized photography experiences are offered separately; access rules protect river roosts.
visitTip: Choose Rowe when the experience itself matters more than flexibility. Reserve well ahead for crane season and follow the sanctuary's current arrival and access instructions.
permit: Follow current Audubon reservation, age and access rules for crane-season experiences
parking: Visitor-center parking for authorized visits; follow current crane-season parking/check-in instructions
accessibility: Contact Rowe Sanctuary for the current accommodation options for the specific experience; transportation assistance is described for some guided tours

name: Fort Kearny Hike-Bike Trail Bridge
type: Public river bridge + state recreation area
summary: A popular self-guided river crossing for watching cranes leave or return to the Platte, with new viewing platforms added to the bridge in 2026.
whatToExpect: A paved hike-bike trail crosses the Platte River. The south bridge reopened in 2026 with eight new viewing platforms designed to improve crane-watching capacity and safety.
visitTip: Allow time to park and walk to the bridge before first light or sunset. This is a state recreation area, so check the current park-entry permit requirement before you go.
permit: Nebraska state park entry permit required
parking: Use Fort Kearny State Recreation Area trail-access parking
accessibility: Paved trail and new viewing platforms improve access; verify current trail conditions and specific mobility needs before travel

name: Windmill State Recreation Area
summary: A practical daytime crane stop near I-80 with a seasonal first-come viewing blind plus full state recreation-area facilities.
whatToExpect: Nebraska Game and Parks operates a seasonal crane-viewing blind annually from March 1 through April 15; the agency says roughly 10 a.m. to sunset is usually best. Camping and other park facilities are also available.
visitTip: Use this when you want a daytime option rather than a dawn/dusk river-roost experience, especially if camping or traveling I-80.
permit: Nebraska state park entry permit required
accessibility: The park has accessible facilities; verify the seasonal viewing blind and route for your specific needs
